scheme_name: Integrated Horticulture Development Program for Tribal Area Farmers (TASP) HRT-3
description:
The Integrated Horticulture Development Program for Tribal Area Farmers is a significant initiative launched by the Government of India under the Tribal Area Sub-Plan (TASP) framework.

This program was introduced in the year 2010 with the aim of enhancing the livelihoods of tribal farmers through the promotion of horticulture.

The primary objective of the program is to increase the income of tribal farmers by providing them with access to improved horticultural practices.

The program specifically targets the cultivation of fruits, vegetables, and spices which are essential for improving nutrition and generating income.

The program aims to cover approximately 1,00,000 hectares of land across various tribal regions in India.

By the year 2025, the program seeks to increase the average income of tribal farmers by at least 30 percent through enhanced horticultural practices.

The benefits of the program include financial assistance for the establishment of orchards and vegetable gardens.

Farmers are provided with a subsidy of up to 50 percent on the cost of planting material and inputs.

The maximum financial assistance available under the program is ₹1 lakh per hectare for fruit crops.

For vegetable cultivation, farmers can receive up to ₹50,000 per hectare as financial support.

The program also includes training sessions for farmers to educate them about modern horticultural techniques.

Farmers are assisted in the procurement of quality seeds and planting materials through government nurseries.

Eligibility criteria for the program include being a member of a Scheduled Tribe.

Farmers must also possess a minimum of 0.5 hectares of land to qualify for the assistance.

The age limit for applicants is set at a minimum of 18 years.

Income criteria stipulate that the annual income of the farmer should not exceed ₹2 lakh.

The application process involves several steps.

Farmers must first approach the local horticulture department office to obtain the application form.

The completed application form must be submitted along with required documents such as proof of tribal status and land ownership.

Additional documents include an income certificate and aadhar card for identity verification.

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by the horticulture department officials.

The officials conduct a field visit to verify the details provided in the application.

After verification, the application is approved based on eligibility criteria.

Farmers are then informed about the approval through a formal letter.

Disbursement of funds occurs in a phased manner.

Initially, 50 percent of the approved amount is released for the purchase of planting material.

The remaining 50 percent is disbursed after the successful establishment of the horticultural project.

The program is implemented by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs in collaboration with state horticulture departments.

Each state has a dedicated nodal officer responsible for overseeing the implementation of the program.

Farmers can contact the local horticulture department for any queries regarding the program.

The program also emphasizes the importance of organic farming practices.

Farmers are encouraged to adopt sustainable agricultural practices to enhance soil health.

Training programs are conducted regularly to update farmers on the latest horticultural techniques.

The program has shown positive results in various states including Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, and Jharkhand.

In Madhya Pradesh, over 10,000 tribal farmers have benefited from the program since its inception.

The state government has reported an increase in the production of fruits and vegetables by 25 percent in the tribal areas.

In Odisha, the program has led to the establishment of over 5,000 hectares of orchards.

The average income of participating farmers in Odisha has increased by ₹30,000 annually.

In Jharkhand, the program has been instrumental in promoting the cultivation of indigenous fruits like mango and guava.

The program also aims to create self-help groups among tribal farmers to enhance collective bargaining power.

These self-help groups are provided with training in financial management and marketing strategies.

Farmers are encouraged to sell their produce directly to consumers to maximize profits.

The program also facilitates the establishment of farmer markets in tribal regions.

These markets provide a platform for farmers to sell their produce at fair prices.

The program is aligned with the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture.

It contributes to the broader goals of improving food security and nutrition in tribal areas.

The program also supports the conservation of traditional horticultural practices.

By promoting indigenous crops, the program helps preserve local biodiversity.

The program is monitored through regular assessments and feedback from participating farmers.

The government conducts impact assessments to evaluate the effectiveness of the program.

These assessments help in making necessary adjustments to improve the program's implementation.

The program has received positive feedback from various stakeholders including farmers and local NGOs.

Farmers have reported improved access to markets and better prices for their produce.

The program has also contributed to the empowerment of women in tribal communities.

Women farmers are encouraged to participate in horticultural activities and benefit from the program.

The program has been instrumental in reducing poverty levels in tribal areas.

By providing financial assistance and training, the program helps farmers become self-sufficient.

The Integrated Horticulture Development Program for Tribal Area Farmers continues to evolve.

It adapts to the changing needs of tribal farmers and incorporates new agricultural technologies.

The government remains committed to supporting the livelihoods of tribal communities through this initiative.

Overall, the program represents a significant step towards sustainable development in tribal areas of India.
